newsitem.title: GERMANY: ATHLETICS-GEBRESELASSIE FRUSTRATED BY SLOW PACEMAKER.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GEBRESELASSIE FRUSTRATED BY SLOW PACEMAKER.

text.p: Ethiopia's Olympic champion Haile Gebreselassie went within 0.55 of a second of his own 3,000 metres world indoor record at the Karlsruhe athletics meeting on Friday.

Gebreselassie, who plans to run the distance at next month's world indoor championships in Paris, ran the last seven laps alone to clock seven minutes 31.27 seconds. His record run of 7:30.72 was set in Stuttgart in February last year.
The time was initially given as 7:31.28 but later amended officially by one hundredth of a second.

The Olympic 10,000 metres champion was unhappy with the efforts of one of his pacemakers. Just before he broke away on his own, the diminutive Gebreselassie was forced to tap his second pacemaker on the shoulder in an effort to get him to pick up speed.
"The first pacemaker was good but the second was too slow and upset my pace," he said. "Last year everything was brilliant but it just didn't work today. I'm still going to run the 3,000 in Paris."

The other highlights of the meeting were 1997 world best performances by Romanian Gabriela Szabo in the women's 1,500 metres (4:08.74) and Cuban Yoelvis Quesada in the men's triple jump (17.38 metres).
American Olympic champion Kenny Harrison had to settle for second place in the triple jump with 16.84.
